Solution

The solution is to use a stack to keep track of the opening brackets and their positions. When we encounter a closing bracket, we check if the top of the stack is the corresponding opening bracket. If it is, we pop it. If it is not, we return the position of the closing bracket. If we finish processing the string and the stack is not empty, we return the position of the last unmatched opening bracket. Here is the implementation: ```python def find_mismatch(s): stack = [] for i, c in enumerate(s): if c in '([{': stack.append((c, i)) elif c in ')]}': if not stack: return i top, pos = stack.pop() if (top == '(' and c != ')') or (top == '[' and c != ']') or (top == '{' and c != '}'): return i if stack: return stack[-1][1] return -1 ``` This function returns the position of the first mismatch, or -1 if there are no mismatches.

Explanation

The algorithm uses a stack to keep track of the opening brackets and their positions. When we encounter a closing bracket, we check if the top of the stack is the corresponding opening bracket. If it is, we pop it. If it is not, we return the position of the closing bracket. If we finish processing the string and the stack is not empty, we return the position of the last unmatched opening bracket. The time complexity is O(n) where n is the length of the string, because we process each character once. The space complexity is O(n) in the worst case, when all characters are opening brackets.

Complexity

Time complexity: O(n) Space complexity: O(n)

Reference

This problem is a classic application of the stack data structure. It is often used in problems involving matching pairs, such as parentheses matching, HTML tag matching, etc.

Test Cases

Here are some test cases: ```python assert find_mismatch("()") == -1 assert find_mismatch("]") == 0 assert find_mismatch("([)]") == 2 assert find_mismatch("{[}]") == 2 assert find_mismatch("(((") == 2 assert find_mismatch("") == -1 assert find_mismatch("({[]})") == -1 assert find_mismatch("({[}])") == 3 ``` These test cases cover various scenarios, including no mismatches, mismatches at the beginning, mismatches in the middle, and mismatches at the end.

Additional Notes

This problem can also be solved using a counter, but the stack approach is more general and can handle nested structures. The counter approach would only work for simple parentheses, not for multiple types of brackets.
